title: Power Toys Run: Calculator doesn't handle scientific notation properly

judgment.rationale: The exact expression deterministically exposes a parser rewrite bug.
evidence: The issue reports =0-1e0 returning 0 instead of -1.
CheckScientificNotation consumes an optional mantissa minus and rewrites the signed token before implicit multiplication.
The analogous Command Palette fix did not modify PowerToys Run.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the narrow PowerToys Run parser fix and regression coverage.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix covers the PowerToys Run calculator implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve binary subtraction around scientific notation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The optional leading minus in CheckScientificNotation can absorb the binary subtraction operator, producing an adjacent numeric-parenthesis expression that later becomes implicit multiplication.
plan: Update CalculateHelper.CheckScientificNotation to match an unsigned mantissa while retaining a signed exponent.
Keep unary minus outside the rewritten scientific literal and verify validation still accepts it.
Add transformation and end-to-end regression cases.
verification: Verify 0-1e0 transforms as 0-(1 * 10^(0)) and evaluates to -1.
Cover -1e0, 1e-3, .1e2, 1.e2, addition, multiplication, whitespace, and culture-normalized decimals.

confidence.rationale: The source transformation reproduces the reported result and the analogous fix establishes the intended boundary.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run binds the subtraction sign to the following scientific-notation literal, so the expression is evaluated as implicit multiplication.
known_information: The reporter supplied =0-1e0, expected -1, actual 0, and a screenshot.
Current Run code permits a leading mantissa minus.
Existing tests omit binary subtraction immediately before scientific notation.
inferences: The mantissa sign likely consumes the binary operator.
A context-aware unary-sign boundary is required.
issue_context.analysis: The failure is reproducible from the current parser rewrite, so no diagnostic archive is needed before design approval.
initial_investigation: Inspected CalculateHelper, CalculateEngine, NumberTranslator, QueryTests, and the related Command Palette fix history.

design.root_cause: CheckScientificNotation matches -1e0 as one token after 0-, then the implicit-multiplication pass changes 0(-1 * 10^(0)) into multiplication.
evidence: Current regex includes an optional mantissa minus.
The following rewrite inserts multiplication between a number and an opening parenthesis.
The issue's exact input reproduces the resulting zero.

affected_files.purpose: Parser transformation and result regression coverage.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The scientific token owns a leading minus.
implementation_steps.change: Match only the unsigned mantissa and preserve unary minus as ordinary expression syntax.
edge_cases: Preserve negative exponents and leading/trailing decimal points.
tests: End-to-end cases for negative exponents and decimal mantissas.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Standalone notation is covered but the operator boundary is not.
implementation_steps.change: Add binary, unary, whitespace, and culture cases.
edge_cases: Run both explicit equals and normal calculator query paths.
tests: Run the existing calculator unit-test project.

verify: Build the PowerToys Run calculator and unit tests in x64 Debug.
Launch PowerToys Run and verify =0-1e0 returns -1 and existing scientific notation remains correct.
risks: Changing the intermediate form of unary negatives could regress validation if not covered.
A broad regex change could affect decimal forms.
alternatives: A full tokenizer is more robust but unnecessarily broad for this isolated defect.
Whitespace-dependent parsing was rejected because it would preserve incorrect behavior for compact expressions.

actions.label: Approve scientific-notation parser design
actions.note: Fork-side implementation only; no upstream action.

non_blocking_notes: Prove both unary-negative and binary-subtraction transformations.
